No, that's not true. The Swiss Confederation did not adopt a constitution in 1291, and no Swiss constitution remains unchanged to this day. 

The origins of the Swiss Confederation are rooted in the Swiss Charter of 1291, a pact among the cantons of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden. However, this was not a modern-style constitution but a feudal agreement. 

Switzerland's first federal constitution was adopted in 1848, and it has been amended multiple times since then. The current federal constitution was last revised in 2000.
